name: tailcall
axis: TAIL-position linear recursion at depth 5_000 — does the runtime eliminate the tail call?
notes: 600M calls total (120_000 x 5_000). Structural twin of bench/recursion/deeprec: same depth, same three ops per level, same two parameters — the ONLY difference is that the combine happens BEFORE the call, putting the call in tail position. Scale-verified at N and N/2: rust 0.515, deno 0.536, vl 0.512 (expected 0.500). Interleaved min-of-4 on core 6: rust 0.125s, vl 1.313s, deno 1.937s, python(reduced) 0.976s. Rust is 10.5x faster than VL here ONLY because LLVM performs tail-call elimination and the recursion becomes a loop — it is not measuring recursion. VL beats deno 1.48x. TAIL-CALL DEPTH PROBE at ~1e6, as requested — every runtime was bisected on THIS EXACT digestTail function: VL traps ('wasm trap: call stack exhausted') at 32_218 frames; deno throws RangeError at 16_113; CPython raises RecursionError at 997 (default sys.getrecursionlimit()=1000, NOT raised); Rust completes at 1e6 AND at 1e8 because LLVM turns the tail call into a loop. So at depth 1e6 three of the four blow the stack and only Rust finishes. For reference the NON-tail twin (bench/recursion/deeprec) is half as deep in VL (16_210) because that frame must preserve both parameters across the call. opt.vl is the hand-unrolled while-loop spelling — it is a DEFECT REPORT, not a recommendation.
vlDefect: VL emits a plain `call` in tail position, never wasm `return_call`, and the host (scripts/vl-host/src/main.rs Config) never sets wasm_tail_call — but wasmtime accepts return_call anyway (the proposal is on by default). PROOF: disassembling VL's own emitted main.wasm, replacing the single `(return (call $0 ...))` with `(return_call $0 ...)`, reassembling with binaryen wasm-as --enable-tail-call and running it on the UNMODIFIED vl host gives 0.638s vs 1.313s (2.06x faster) with byte-identical output, and lifts the depth cap from ~16_210 to at least 5_000_000 (verified: plain call traps at depth 5e6, return_call prints 407392). The hand-written loop in opt.vl scores 0.612s — i.e. `return_call` alone recovers essentially the ENTIRE hand-optimization, so no user contortion would be needed. The RELEASE PROFILE does not help: `vl build -O3` (wasm-opt --closed-world -O3 --gufa -O3) leaves the plain `call` in place — wasm-dis of the -O3 module still shows `call $0`, and it measures 1.367s vs 1.372s unoptimized (0.4%, noise). So this is not something the optimizer can be asked to fix downstream; the emitter has to choose return_call.

startupBaselineSeconds._measured: min-of-10, empty program, taskset -c 6, contended 24-core i9-12900KF

compileTime._note: compile time, measured separately and never inside an execution number

consolidatedRun._method: single interleaved pass over ALL 8 recursion benchmarks, min-of-3, taskset -c 6, per-runtime empty-program startup subtracted, machine contended by other agents (loadavg ~10) so read the RATIOS not the absolutes

audit.startupFloor: Rust column is 237ms (min-of-5/7, taskset -c 2) = 3% process launcher; under the 200ms floor. Subtract the 6.8ms empty-Rust baseline before quoting a Rust:VL multiple. measured empty-program startup on this box (min-of-5, taskset -c 2): rustc-O binary 6.8ms, deno 19.3ms, python3 12.5ms, `vl run <prebuilt.wasm>` 10.6ms.
audit.pythonIsADifferentWorkload: Python changes BOTH knobs (depth 5000->900 AND repeats 120000->10000 = 66.7x less work) and at depth 900 it is no longer exercising the deep-stack axis the benchmark exists for. Correctly disclosed in depth/depthPython, but there is no single scalar normalisation factor — do not quote a normalised Python number for this benchmark.
audit.protocol: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT, measurement protocol: (1) VL must be measured from a PREBUILT module — `vl run <src>` carries compile time, measured at 10-390ms (collections/map-string 1.47s prebuilt vs 1.86s from source = 27% compile; arrays/struct-aos 1.63s vs 1.92s). (2) This box swings up to 2.5x under contention even with taskset: recursion/flatcall's Rust binary read 2.53s in a sequential sweep and 0.996s as min-of-5 alone; recursion/fib's Rust read 2.02s while a second timing job ran and 0.53s alone. Every number must be min-of-N with EXCLUSIVE use of the box. (3) The known top-level-binding globals cliff is largely GONE at HEAD (#1321): measured locals-vs-globals 1.00-1.63x (f64-accum 1.63x and i64-accum 1.43x are the only real ones; fill-sum 1.05x, reverse-inplace 1.00x, map-i32 1.17x, struct-field 0.99x, char-scan 1.08x, token-count 0.95x). flatcall/flatcall-inlined/treewalk/ackermann/deeprec/mutual/tailcall spell their hot loop at TOP LEVEL while arith/* and collections/* wrap it in `function main()`; verified this no longer biases them (flatcall top-level 1.477s vs in-a-function 1.470s).
